key_insight: Optimizing the training scenarios themselves can improve climate emulator generalization more than simply adding more standard emissions pathways.
engineering_relevance: For compute-limited climate modeling, a small set of dynamically rich scenarios may deliver higher-value training data for building more accurate surrogate models.
method: Use a differentiable simple climate model to estimate how emulator loss changes with training-data perturbations.
Iteratively modify scenarios to maximize emulator skill and structural diversity.
Train and test emulators on optimized scenarios, then validate transfer to an intermediate-complexity climate model.
evidence_signal: An emulator trained on one optimized scenario outperformed another trained on six standard ScenarioMIP pathways, and optimized SCM-driven scenarios also produced a more skillful emulator than ScenarioMIP outputs in a higher-fidelity model.
watch_item: The optimization depends on a differentiable SCM and may not transfer identically to all climate models or real-world forcing uncertainties.
paper_title: Optimal scenario design for climate emulation
